title: CO2-to-methanol reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed thermal-catalyst family for CO2-to-methanol screening. These routes are reference starting points for cost, route maturity, and evidence quality rather than exact commercial recipes.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance economics, evidence quality, route maturity, and reported performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward catalyst cost while keeping route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward transparent pricing anchors and more defensible preparation routes.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2019
citations.note: Study of ternary Cu-ZnO-ZrO2 interactions, with binary controls; not a measured Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 recipe.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2021
citations.note: Ni-promoted indium-oxide route showing how interfacial metal promotion can raise methanol productivity.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2022
citations.note: Photothermocatalytic CO2-to-CO study on In-embedded In2O3; mechanistic context only, not direct methanol-performance evidence.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2022
citations.note: Pd-In2O3-ZrO2 catalyst architecture reported with sustained methanol selectivity under CO2 hydrogenation.

citations.label: Nature Catalysis 2024
citations.note: Cu/ZrOx cluster route on MgO showing strong methanol productivity without moving to a noble-metal basis.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2025
citations.note: Inverse In2O3-x/Ni interfacial route showing how reconstructed In-Ni motifs can stabilize methanol-selective sites.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2025
citations.note: ZnO nanorod-based methanol route emphasizing geometry-sensitive CO2 activation and oxygen-vacancy exposure.

citations.label: Science 2012
citations.note: Behrens, Studt et al.: identification of the active site of methanol synthesis over the industrial Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalyst via combined microscopy and DFT.

citations.label: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2016
citations.note: Kattel, Yan, Yang and Liu: optimising binding energies of key intermediates for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol over oxide-supported copper catalysts.

citations.label: Nat. Commun. 2019
citations.note: Nominal 0.75 wt% Pd/In2O3 prepared by co-precipitation sustained 0.96 gMeOH/(h gcat) with 78% methanol selectivity after 500 h at 553 K, 5 MPa, H2/CO2=4 and WHSV 48000 cm3(STP)/(h gcat) in the 2019 study.

citations.label: Appl. Catal. B 2017
citations.note: Pd/In2O3 with oxygen-vacancy engineering: 20% CO2 conversion, ~70% methanol selectivity at 573 K and 5 MPa.

route_templates.name: Cu-Zn-Al co-precipitation route
route_templates.route_note: Closest screening proxy to conventional Cu/Zn/Al methanol catalyst manufacture and the easiest basis to defend commercially.

route_templates.name: Cu-ZrOx interface route
preprocess: Narrow precipitation or deposition window setup
route_templates.route_note: The cited Cu/ZrOx-MgO study uses liquid-phase ALD. Its 14/21/65 wt% representation and generic processing chain are unvalidated screening proxies; ALD-specific processing cost is not estimated.

route_templates.name: In2O3-ZrO2 low-temperature route
route_templates.route_note: Low-temperature methanol route with strong literature momentum, but indium inventory discipline and oxide-state control keep maturity below Cu baselines.

candidates.title: Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 baseline
candidates.summary: Industrial copper-zinc-alumina basis for CO2-to-methanol catalyst cost screening.
decision_notes: Best anchor for practical methanol screening because copper exposure stays visible and the route maps well onto established oxide-catalyst manufacturing.
Performance is not the family leader, but route maturity and reproducibility are the strongest.

pricing.note: Live Cu feed with a mild precursor conversion markup for copper-oxide catalyst manufacture.
USGS MCS 2026 North American SHG zinc, 2025e $1.49/lb, x 0.803 Zn mass fraction of ZnO = $1.20/lb contained-metal floor; oxide conversion cost not included.
2025 USGS alumina import value used as a bulk oxide support proxy.

candidates.title: Cu/ZrOx-MgO interface route
candidates.summary: Cu route that trades extra support/interface discipline for higher methanol productivity at moderate metal cost.
decision_notes: Useful when Cu economics still matter but the baseline CZA route leaves too much performance on the table.
Route overhead is higher because zirconia/basic-support contact and interface stability need tighter control.
The cited Cu/ZrOx-MgO study uses liquid-phase ALD. Its 14/21/65 wt% representation and generic processing chain are unvalidated screening proxies; ALD-specific processing cost is not estimated.

pricing.note: Live Cu feed retained as the dominant traded-metal term.

Zirconia-side support term uses a conservative engineering proxy because a direct bulk public price was not verified in this pass. USGS MCS 2026 zircon (2025e ~$1,900/t imported, ~66% ZrO2) implies ~$1.31/lb contained ZrO2, corroborating this proxy as a floor.

Basic support term held on a conservative engineering proxy to avoid reagent-pack distortion. UN Comtrade 2024 magnesia imports (HS 251990) averaged $0.52/kg (China $0.39/kg; high-purity flows to $4.10/kg), bracketing this proxy from below; Sigma 342793 lab price ($0.38/g) is the packaged ceiling.

candidates.title: In2O3-ZrO2 low-temperature route
candidates.summary: Indium-oxide route that targets high methanol selectivity at lower temperature but carries meaningful indium price pressure.
decision_notes: Best fit when methanol selectivity at lower temperature is worth paying for a scarcer oxide system.
Indium inventory and oxide-state control keep this route less mature than Cu-led baselines.
Cited Ni/Pd-promoted and flame-made oxide systems provide architectural context. They do not validate this 55 wt% elemental-In/45 wt% ZrO2 recipe, temperature window, or assigned performance score.

pricing.note: 2025 USGS refined-indium price used as the bulk indium term for indium-oxide methanol screening.

Zirconia term remains a conservative engineering proxy pending a cleaner public bulk quote. USGS MCS 2026 zircon (2025e ~$1,900/t imported, ~66% ZrO2) implies ~$1.31/lb contained ZrO2, corroborating this proxy as a floor.

candidates.title: Pd/In2O3 promoted oxide
candidates.summary: Nominal 0.75 wt% Pd/In2O3 prepared by co-precipitation sustained 0.96 gMeOH/(h gcat) with 78% methanol selectivity after 500 h at 553 K, 5 MPa, H2/CO2=4 and WHSV 48000 cm3(STP)/(h gcat) in the 2019 study.
decision_notes: The performance ceiling of the oxide branch; indium inventory, not palladium, dominates the material term.
Co-precipitation is source-supported; the reused Cu-Zn-Al processing chain and its labels are a costing proxy, not the reported Pd/In2O3 recipe.

pricing.note: Live Pd feed with a precursor markup; 0.75 wt% loading is source-quoted.
2025 USGS refined indium $176.90/lb x 0.829 In mass fraction of In2O3 = $146.65/lb contained-metal floor; oxide conversion cost not included.
